narrative.overview:
A desktop operations workspace for pilots to join a community FSD server, monitor the Aerofly bridge, and handle a flight plan, transponder, and messages. The deep flight context uses flat blue-charcoal surfaces, a cyan primary action, and text alongside every status color.

The connection path is explicit and the connected view separates aircraft state from flight-plan and messaging tasks. At compact widths, the two-column flight deck becomes a single scrollable column. Advanced endpoint and proxy settings stay behind an explicit disclosure.
keyCharacteristics: Deep blue-charcoal default theme with a matching high-contrast light theme.
Segoe UI for labels and forms; Consolas only for the transponder measurement.
One-pixel borders and tonal surface changes; no decorative shadows.
Full-text navigation and connection actions across Simplified Chinese, Hong Kong Traditional Chinese, and American English.

rules.name: Status-in-Words
rules.body: State colors always appear with a readable label.

rules.name: Server-Address Rule
rules.body: Show community servers as complete host:port addresses.

dos: Do show connection state, telemetry state, and transponder mode as text as well as color.
Do keep the primary connection action visually distinct from server-management controls.
Do keep form labels above fields and align paired columns to a common baseline.
donts: Don't expose internal ECO or TYPE abbreviations as user-facing labels.
Don't seed Sweatbox as a normal community-flight server.
Don't make a VATSIM endpoint look like approval to connect with this client.
Don't use a glyph alone for delete, connection, or emergency actions.
